title: Real Estate Joint Venture Agreement
summary: A capital partner and an operating partner team up on one property: who funds, who works, how profits are split, and how it ends.
useWhen: One party brings the money (or credit) and the other finds, renovates, manages or sells a specific property.
watchOuts: Passive money partners: if one party contributes only money and relies on the other's efforts, the arrangement may be a security (an investment contract) under federal and state law. Many sponsors use an LLC and exemptions with counsel.
Put title in an entity, or record the JV's interest. A partner holding title alone can sell or mortgage the property without the other's knowledge.
Renovation work may require a contractor's license. Selling the property for the JV may require a real estate license if a partner is paid a commission.
Define the budget, overrun funding and the sale or refinance trigger. Most JV disputes come from cost overruns and disagreements about when to sell.
Tax: an unincorporated JV is usually a partnership for tax purposes (Form 1065). Flips may be taxed as ordinary income.

sections.title: 1. Partners and property
sections.body:
**Capital partner:** {{capital_name}}, {{capital_address}} ({{capital_email}})

**Operating partner:** {{operator_name}}, {{operator_address}} ({{operator_email}})

The partners form a joint venture for the property at {{property_address}} (the "Property"). Strategy: {{strategy}}. Effective {{effective_date}}.

sections.title: 2. Title
sections.body: The Property will be held by {{title_holder}}. Neither partner may sell, mortgage or lease the Property except as this agreement allows.

sections.title: 3. Contributions
4. Management
sections.body: Operating partner manages the day-to-day project, hires licensed and insured contractors, obtains permits, and keeps Capital partner informed with weekly updates and photos. Operating partner may spend up to {{spend_limit}} per item within the budget. These need both partners' written approval: changes to the budget or scope over 10%, any loan or lien, the listing price and any sale or lease, any contract with a partner's affiliate, and any decision outside the strategy.

sections.title: 5. Money and records
sections.body: All venture money goes through a separate bank account in the venture's name, with both partners having online access. Each partner may inspect the books at any time. Operating partner will provide a final accounting within 30 days after the sale or refinance.

sections.title: 6. Distributions
sections.body:
Net proceeds from sale, refinance or operations will be distributed in this order:
1. Repay venture debts and costs of sale.
2. Return each partner's cash capital contributions, including overrun capital.
3. Pay Capital partner a preferred return of {{pref_return}}% per year on unreturned capital, if stated.
4. Split the remaining profit: Capital partner {{split_capital}}%, Operating partner {{split_operator}}%.

sections.title: 7. Timeline and exit
sections.body: Target timeline: {{timeline}}. If the Property has not been sold or refinanced by {{exit_trigger}}, Capital partner may require that it be listed for sale with a licensed broker at a price recommended by the broker, or may buy out Operating partner's interest at the value established by an independent appraisal, minus selling costs.

sections.title: 8. Operating partner's promises
sections.body: Operating partner will act in good faith, put the venture's interest first, disclose any relationship with contractors or buyers, and not take any undisclosed fee, kickback or markup. If a partner is a licensed real estate agent and will earn a commission, it must be disclosed and approved in writing.

sections.title: 9. Insurance and liability
sections.body: The venture will carry builder's risk or vacant-property insurance and liability insurance, with both partners or the venture as named insureds. Each partner indemnifies the other for losses caused by its own negligence, fraud or breach.

sections.title: 10. Default and removal
sections.body: If Operating partner abandons the project or materially breaches this agreement and does not cure within 15 days after notice, Capital partner may take over management, hire a replacement, and deduct the cost from Operating partner's share of profits.

sections.title: 11. Securities and taxes
sections.body: The partners intend for both to participate actively in major decisions. They have been advised that if one partner is a passive investor, securities laws may apply. The venture will file any required tax returns. Each partner pays its own income taxes.

sections.title: 12. Disputes
sections.body: The partners will negotiate in good faith, then mediate, before litigation.

sections.title: 13. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything. Creative-finance transactions (subject-to, seller financing, wraps, lease-options, contracts for deed) can trigger lender due-on-sale rights, federal and state lending and licensing laws (Truth in Lending/Dodd-Frank, SAFE Act), state executory-contract statutes and consumer-protection claims. Each party, and especially the seller, should have independent legal counsel and a tax adviser before signing.
